Week 8 · A1 · Beginner

Mon, ma, mes

The possessive matches the thing owned, not the owner: sa sœur can mean his sister or her sister.

Pick an owner and a family member. Watch the copper possessive follow the noun’s gender.

Choose by owner, then match the noun’s gender and number.

First pick the owner (my, your, his …). Then choose the form that matches the noun: masculine, feminine or plural. That is why sa mère means both “his mother” and “her mother”: sa is feminine because mère is, not because of who owns her. One exception to remember: before a feminine noun that starts with a vowel, use mon, ton, son: mon amie, never ma amie.

Pattern

Ownermasculinefeminineplural
je (my)mon frèrema sœurmes parents
tu (your)ton frèreta sœurtes parents
il / elle (his, her)son frèresa sœurses parents
nous (our)notre frèrenotre sœurnos parents
vous (your)votre frèrevotre sœurvos parents
ils / elles (their)leur frèreleur sœurleurs parents

Examples

No French voice was found on this device, so the ▶ écouter buttons are hidden.

  • Mon frère habite à Kumasi. My brother lives in Kumasi.
  • Ta mère est très gentille. Your mother is very kind.
  • Paul cherche ses clés. Paul is looking for his keys.
  • Nos enfants vont à l’école ici. Our children go to school here.
  • Où est votre passeport, monsieur ? Where is your passport, sir?

Common mistakes

  • ma amie → mon amie. Before a vowel, ma/ta/sa become mon/ton/son.
  • Marie aime son mère. → Marie aime sa mère. mère is feminine; it doesn’t matter that Marie is a woman.
  • leur enfants → leurs enfants. Several children: add the -s.
  • With polite vous, use votre / vos, even for one person.

Quiz

Parler: your family

A1 goal: introduce yourself and talk about your day in short, simple sentences. Describe four people in your family: Ma mère s’appelle … Mon frère habite à … Mes parents sont … Mon amie …
